sources.outlet: T. Rowe Price Associates, Form 13F-HR via SEC EDGAR
sources.quote: Form 13F Information Table Value Total: 864,926,710 (round to nearest dollar)
sources.searcher_note: The primary filing the lead cites (Q1 2026, 4,549 entries): cover total $864,926,710 under a 'nearest dollar' label. The filing itself; not coverage and not a finding. T. Rowe's Q2 2026 13F-HR (filed 2026-08-14) shows 999,124,702, the same scale. EDGAR lists no 13F-HR/A from T. Rowe for 2026.

sources.outlet: Barclays PLC, Form 13F-HR/A via SEC EDGAR
sources.quote: All values were previously reported in denominations of thousands and have been updated in this amendment to reflect exact dollar values in accordance with Form 13F requirements.
sources.searcher_note: Same error, different filer: in Feb-Mar 2026 Barclays refiled every quarter from 2022-12-31 to 2025-09-30 (13 amendments per EDGAR) to convert thousands to dollars. StockTitan summarized these amendments, but its pages block scripted fetch.

sources.quote: Legacy systems that still round to thousands are producing non-compliant filings.
sources.searcher_note: A vendor's general claim that thousands-unit filings keep happening; no counts, no filer names.

sources.quote: The failure is silent: nothing in the XML flags the unit.
sources.searcher_note: Data-user guide. It treats the filing date as the only reliable signal ('On or after January 3, 2023 Whole dollars Use the value as filed'), which assumes post-2023 filings are clean, the opposite of the lead's finding. Offers an implied-price check that would catch it. Modified 2026-07-31.

sources.quote: The requirement starting January 3, 2023 to round to the nearest dollar represents a change from the prior requirement to round such values to the nearest thousand dollars.
sources.searcher_note: Explainer on the rule; not a finding.

notes: No news or research found reporting that hundreds of post-2023 13F reports still use thousands, or naming T. Rowe Price for it. The closest known-pattern evidence is Barclays' own 2026 amendments. Two sources are EDGAR filings, read on the SEC site as primary records rather than found through a web search. Memory: none relevant.
